message.reasoning:
I need to respond to a trade offer in Monopoly.

Reviewing my holdings. I have cash of $500 and several mortgaged properties. I notice a discrepancy: I mortgaged Indiana, Electric, Water, and Vermont to build houses, but all properties currently show zero houses.

I recall building one house on each orange property. The game state shows zero houses and $500 cash, which conflicts with my memory of having $200 after collecting rent. I am unsure whether the build failed or the state is simply outdated.

The $28 rent collected from p2 on Tennessee matches the unimproved monopoly rate, not the $70 rate for one house. This confirms my houses were sold or reset between turns.

The timeline shows no BUILD event. I only mortgaged properties and never actually constructed houses.

The timeline confirms I mortgaged Indiana, Electric, Water, and Vermont in turn 74 and ended without building. I had roughly $472 after those mortgages, not the $172 I recalled from my private notes.

The $500 cash balance checks out exactly. It equals the $472 remaining after mortgages plus the $28 rent collected this turn.

Virginia was traded to p4. That player now holds States and Virginia. They still need St. Charles from p3.

p4 also owns Marvin Gardens and North Carolina. They need either Atlantic or Pacific. Pacific is owned by p2. Atlantic is unowned.

Dark blue is split between p3 and p4.

p2 has incomplete light blue and yellow monopolies. p3 owns all four railroads plus St. Charles, Illinois, and Park Place.

The offer is $130 cash for my mortgaged Vermont Avenue. The buyer would inherit the mortgage and could pay 10% interest to keep it unmortgaged.

Vermont's unmortgage would cost $55. p2 still needs Oriental to complete light blue, so this trade does not finish their set. I am weighing whether $130 is fair for a mortgaged property that blocks a weak set.

The $130 offer is effectively a good deal for me. A mortgaged property does not return its mortgage value, so the buyer would need to pay an extra $55 to unmortgage it.

Strategically, keeping Vermont blocks p2 from completing light blue. That set is weak, but p2 has $1272 in cash and could build once they acquire Oriental.

I am calculating the house costs for my orange properties. One house on each of St. James, Tennessee, and New York costs $300, leaving $200 cash. Two houses on two properties and one on the third would cost $500, leaving no buffer. I should not sell Vermont if keeping it blocks p2 from completing light blue, since I have enough cash to build houses instead.

I am now calculating the exact cash implications of the trade. $130 would let me build one house on each orange property, leaving a $200 buffer. Two houses on two properties and one on the third would cost $500, leaving only $130 after the sale. That is too thin against the $200 rent from p3's four railroads.

The real question is whether to accept the offer. The immediate benefit is the extra cash for building. The downside is that Vermont does not complete any set for me, and p2 still needs Oriental to finish light blue.

The $130 offer is a clear overpay. The buyer would need to pay $55 in interest to unmortgage the property, making it effectively worth $185.

I am now comparing the rent potential of light blue with three houses against orange. Orange's St. James rent with houses reaches $750, which dwarfs light blue's $270.

I am now questioning whether blocking p2 from completing light blue is worth $130. p2 has no monopolies and only $1272 in cash, so they are the weakest player. p3 owns all four railroads plus Park Place, St. Charles, and Illinois, making them the real threat. My earlier strategic note to keep Vermont was written when I lacked a monopoly and had less cash.

I have decided to reject the trade. The $130 offer is not worth giving up a permanent block on p2's light blue set, and I already have enough cash to build houses.

I considered raising the counter-offer to $250 or $300, but p2 still needs Oriental to complete light blue, so they may not pay much more.

I am now considering a counter-offer of $200 to $250. I have no houses on any property right now.

I cannot build until I respond to this trade. I will reject the offer and keep Vermont as a block. p2 has no properties I want, so raising the counter-offer is pointless.

I realized that $130 is far too little to reach three houses on all orange properties. That requires $900 total, so I would still need roughly $400 more cash. Even a counter-offer of $250 or $300 would only get me to two houses on two properties and one on the third, leaving me short of the power spike at three houses. This makes the trade offer practically useless for building.

The mortgage transfer means the $130 offer is effectively worth $180 total, since the original $50 mortgage is already paid. This makes the trade a strong financial deal despite the strategic cost of blocking p2's light blue set.

I will reject the offer outright. I considered a higher counter-offer as a poison pill, but p2 has no properties I need and would simply waste an exchange.
